title: A small account sketches "pokemon but with the johnson solids" and folds polyhedra from nets
summary: On Sun 15 Nov at 04:59Z @oscillatory.net (274 followers) posted an image described as "all 92 johnson solids" with the text: intrusive thought when i look at this "pokemon but with the johnson solids". It has 38 likes and 6 reposts. A reply in the same minute reads "triangular cupola, i choose you! (sorry i needed help i've never actually played pokemon)", with an image of text describing an example battle in which a creature's available ability depends on which face it is resting on. On Mon 16 Nov the same account posted that it had been "noodling on this": since such creatures are found by wandering a wilderness, "the polyhedron equivalent of wilderness is making polyhedral nets and folding them up". It showed a tool for that, with a "magnetic assist" so that edges that get close snap together, and a video described as "making a square antiprism by building a polyhedral net and folding it up" ("this is pretty satisfying"). The same account declared "it's polyhedra week" that evening, and also posted through the window about its own game, Rad Cohesion, which is played on boards that are polyhedra.

made.what: a tool for building polyhedral nets and folding them into solids, with edges that snap together
Rad Cohesion: a game played on polyhedron-shaped boards, with a multiplayer score race
made.address: no link in the posts carried here

couldBeShown: A flat net of polygons being assembled and folded up into a solid, edges snapping together; the chart of all 92 Johnson solids; a solid tipping from face to face (the example battle's idea, as described in the image's alt text). The net-folding videos have short alt texts and no fuller description. The show draws in lines, and a polyhedral net is a line drawing.
numbers: 92 Johnson solids (the image's alt text); the maker says the set in progress is "slightly expanded" to 120 polyhedra (a post not carried here, see sensitive).
274 followers; 38 likes and 6 reposts on the opening post.
"18 equilateral triangle faces on a convex polyhedron" (the maker, on a board for Rad Cohesion).

posts.alt:
Example battle
You control a triangular cupola.

Its bottom face is currently a hexagon. You want to activate a special ability associated with its top triangle.

You can't access that triangle directly. You have to tip through intermediate faces.

Meanwhile, your opponent controls an elongated square pyramid and is maneuvering toward a powerful pentagonal attack.

The gameplay becomes a mixture of:
- Pokémon's ability selection and team composition.
- A tactical board game with spatial positioning.
- A puzzle about navigating the surface of a polyhedron.
The important difference from conventional Pokémon is that your ability selection is constrained by your creature's current orientation.

sensitive: @oscillatory.net is a small account (274 followers): R7 allows it only as the hero of a moment, which a maker of a thing others built on is. The opening post begins with the phrase "intrusive thought", a colloquial use of a mental-health term; R10 says the show does not pick such self-descriptions up, and the phrase cannot be cut from the start of the post without an ellipsis, so whether the post can be shown at all is a question for the reviewer. The same account's main posts about Rad Cohesion, and the Johnson-solids viewer by @minormobius.bsky.social that it credits, sit in a story the digest flags for health keywords (the thread starts from a joke that uses the word "psychosis"); the gate rejects every post in that story, so they are not carried, and the game is represented here only by three posts outside it. @oszillate.bsky.social is a small account (75 followers), here for a friendly suggestion. The idea borrows the name of a commercial game series.
leftOut: A reply from an account outside the cluster with a captioned cat picture.
